title: The Height Signal
text:
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(2409)
n <- 20000
position <- sample(
  c("Middle blocker", "Outside hitter", "Setter", "Libero"),
  n,
  replace = TRUE,
  prob = c(.22, .34, .18, .26)
)
position_mean <- c("Middle blocker" = 74, "Outside hitter" = 72,
                   "Setter" = 71, "Libero" = 67)
position_effect <- c("Middle blocker" = .75, "Outside hitter" = .45,
                     "Setter" = .15, "Libero" = -.30)
height <- rnorm(n, position_mean[position], 2.4)
performance <- 50 + position_effect[position] * (height - 70) +
  rnorm(n, 0, 10)

players <- data.frame(
  height = height,
  performance = pmax(1, pmin(99, performance)),
  position = factor(position, levels = names(position_mean))
)

ggplot(players, aes(height, performance, colour = position)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .16, size = .7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE,
              linewidth = 1.2, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~position, ncol = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#e76f51", "#087f8c", "#e9b949", "#6c63a8")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(58, 84, 4)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 20)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(58, 84), ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "Player height (inches)",
    y = "Composite performance score"
  ) +
  guides(colour = "none") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#f5f0e8", colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#fffdf8", colour = NA),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#d9d4ca", linewidth = .35),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#132a2f", colour = NA),
    strip.text = element_text(colour = "#fffdf8", face = "bold"),
    panel.spacing = unit(1.2, "lines"),
    plot.caption = element_text(colour = "#5f7374")
  )







Figure 1: Each point is one simulated player-season observation. Height is measured in inches; performance is a composite of kills, blocks, digs, and aces, standardized within position.





This graphic uses simulated observations to show the intended shape of the analysis. The real project should replace the simulation with collected player-level data before making claims about college volleyball.
